footnotes:
Krickeberg & Rauch 1976 date this instrument "17. Jahrhundert" (citing Sachs 1922, col. 228), yet they also note
that Friedrich Ehe became master in 1692. Langwill 1993 gives Friedrich's Ehe's dates as 1669-1743, and says he
flourished 1692-1743. Langwill further notes that some instruments marked "Friedrich Ehe" may be by his son, Martin
Friedrich (1714-79, fl. 1742-79). If the instrument is by the father, Friedrich Ehe, an approximate date of "early 18c"
seems plausible. It is unclear why Krickeberg & Rauch 1976 offer so little detail on the instrument in comparison with
other trombones in their catalogue, unless certain details were lost when the instrument was restored. The few details
they provide relating to the instrument are taken from Sachs 1922.

According to Krickeberg & Rauch 1976. Apparently the instrument was complete in 1922 when Sachs prepared his
catalog.
maker: Bell section only, Friedrich Ehe, Nuremberg
